# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-17 (Extended v130)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 5—Louis Philippe's reign)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Rue de la Verrerie (Courfeyrac's residence); Faubourg Saint-Antoine; Faubourg Saint-Marceau; wine-shops (Seven Billiards on Rue des Mathurins-Saint-Jacques; Corinthe on Rue Mondétour; Richefeu's at Barrière du Maine; Café Musain); schools; English provincial towns (Dunstead harbor town, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt, Quenford). **Environmental details**: Frost silvered hedges overnight; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; rain threatened; wind carries salt/tar scent; bees hum in lavender; children chase hoop down lane; road ruts and puddles after thaw; smoke from chimneys lies flat; gulls quarrel over fish heads in harbor/steps; bells ring for vespers; light goes early; river up in spring; baker's boy often late; lines at oven grow long. Dogs bark at nothing. Clouds predicted rain, wrongly.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, charcoal sketches, moisture. Fireplace with red-hot brazier. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo**: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy). Rope-ladder with hooks, verdigris candlestick.

**WINE-SHOPS & MEETING PLACES**: Centers of revolutionary fermentation. **Seven Billiards (Rue des Mathurins-Saint-Jacques)** and **Café Rue Saint-Hyacinthe**: student rallying points. **Corinthe (Rue Mondétour)**: young men assemble; secret and public meetings. **Richefeu's (Barrière du Maine)**: marble-workers, painters, journeymen sculptors meet 12-1 o'clock; cooling off, playing dominoes. **Café Musain**: Société des Amis de l'A B C affiliated to Mutualists and Cougourde of Aix.

**PARISIAN FIELD (DUNSTEAD area)**: Green meadow with tightly stretched lines, rags drying in wind, old market-gardener's house (Louis XIII era), great roof with dormer windows, dilapidated palisades, water amid poplar-trees. Horizon shows Panthéon, Deaf-Mutes pole, Val-de-Grâce (black, squat, fantastic), Notre Dame towers. Only picturesque spot in monotonous chain of Parisian boulevards.

**FAUBOURG SAINT-ANTOINE CHARACTERISTICS**: Peopled like ant-hill, laborious, courageous, angry as hive of bees. Quivering with expectation. Poignant distress hidden under attic roofs. Dangerous when distress and intelligence meet at extremes. Powder-house of suffering and ideas.

## Marius Pontmercy: Psychological and Financial Crisis
**Identity and background**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's instruction regarding Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Recognized Thénardier in Waterloo painting.

**The Ambush Crisis (resolved with escape)**: Jondrette/Thénardier plotted extortion via Cosette. M. Leblanc escaped: unscrewed coin piece, used as saw to cut cords, brandished red-hot chisel above head emitting threatening glow. **While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty.** Dashed from window. Javert positioned outside with men; took action before Marius's signal. Thénardier woman hurled enormous paving-stone at Javert's head; Javert ducked; stone struck wall. Javert bore off prisoners in three hackney-coaches.

**Marius's aftermath (April Year 4)**: Relocated to Courfeyrac at Rue de la Verrerie for political reasons; paid quarterly rent, vacated hovel. Two reasons: (1) horror of wicked poor man development; (2) avoid lawsuit testimony against Thénardier. Recognized M. Leblanc as Monsieur Fabre (Cosette's biological father). Cosette believed Valjean her father, became convent scholar.

**Current financial crisis (Spring Year 5)**: **First time in life, Marius borrowed five francs from Courfeyrac.** Poverty returned; felt icy breath. Discontinued work—dangerous habit vanishing, difficult to resume. Old coat becoming impossible; new coat growing old; shirts wearing out; hat wearing out; boots giving out. **"If I could but see her once again before I die!"**

**Psychological state—Reverie vs. Reason**: Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. One no longer emerges from self except to dream—idle production, tumultuous stagnant gulf. As labor diminishes, needs increase. Man in reverie generally prodigal and slack; unstrung mind cannot hold life within close bounds. **Yet reason not deranged.** Lost faculty of working and moving firmly toward fixed goal, but endowed with more clear-sightedness and rectitude than ever. Surveyed by calm and real light what passed before eyes; pronounced just criticism with honest dejection and candid disinterestedness. Judgment almost wholly disassociated from hope, held itself aloof and soared on high. **Happy, even in midst of anguish, is he to whom God has given a soul worthy of love and of unhappiness!**

**Marius and Cosette relationship—Memory and hope**: Memory of absent being kindles in darkness of heart; more it has disappeared, more it beams. She—that was Marius's whole thought. One sweet idea alone left: she had loved him; her glance told him so; she did not know his name, but she knew his soul. **In inexplicable hours, though he had no reasons but sadness, he felt obscure quiver of joy: "It is her thoughts that are coming to me!"** Pure, impersonal, ideal reveries fell upon notebook. He called this "writing to her." **Periodical five francs a double riddle**: to Courfeyrac who lent, to unknown recipient who received them.

## Enjolras and Revolutionary Leadership (Spring Year 5)
**Enjolras as nexus of fermentation**: Walking toward organizing mission, reviewed situation. Descried luminous uplifting beneath gloomy skirts of future. **Believed moment at hand**: people taking possession of right; revolution majestically taking France, saying to world: "The sequel to-morrow!" Furnace being heated. Had powder train of friends scattered all over Paris.

**Composed network**: Collaborators include Combeferre (philosophical, penetrating eloquence), Feuilly (cosmopolitan enthusiasm), Courfeyrac (dash), Bahorel (smile), Jean Prouvaire (melancholy), Joly (science), Bossuet (sarcasms). Created sort of electric spark taking fire nearly everywhere. **Result would answer to effort.**

## Jean Valjean
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence.

## Revolutionary Fermentation and Secret Societies (Spring Year 5)
**Public agitation and cartridge-making (April Year 4)**: Workmen openly proclaim cartridge-making. Police raids: April 5, arrested Pardon at five o'clock morning while preparing cartridges. Weapons transfer documented. **Proclamation by wine-merchant Burtot**: "Our doctrines are trammelled, our proclamations torn, our bill-stickers spied upon. Action or reaction. On day when we cease to suit you, break us."**

**Suspicious activities (April 4, Year 4)**: Passer-by mounted post, shouted: "I am a Babouvist!" Workman warned by "very well dressed man": "Don't be alarmed, I am an agent of the committee."

**Discovered documents**: Package on bench near Austerlitz bridge: two printed dialogues signed _Lahautière_, song "Workmen, band together," tin box full cartridges. Ditch between Père-Lachaise and Barrière du Trône: bag with bullet-mould, wooden punch, wooden bowl with hunting-powder grains, cast-iron pot with melted lead traces. **Carpenter found cipher document**: Q, C, D, E with instruction "Learn this list by heart." Letters meant quinturions, centurions, decurions, éclaireurs [scouts]; date u og a' fe = April 15, Year 4.

**Secret society network**: Associations of Friends of People → Society of Rights of Man → Society of Action (impatient individuals breaking away). Other associations: Gallic Society; committee of organization of Municipalities; associations for liberty of press, individual liberty, instruction against indirect taxes; Society of Equal Workingmen (levellers, communists, reformers); Army of Bastilles (military cohort, Venice-stamped genius).

**Military infiltration**: Counted on: fifty-second regiment, fifth, eighth, thirty-seventh, twentieth light cavalry. Burgundy and southern towns: planted liberty tree. Schools moved as faubourgs. **Network spreading like membranes.** Not a point in Paris nor France exempt.

## Historical Context: Louis Philippe and Restoration
**Bourbon Restoration critique**: House of Bourbon returned after Napoleon; believed it bestowed rights, could take back charter rights. Did not understand French society's roots in nation, not Bourbons.

**Fifteen years intellectual progress (1815-1830)**: Great principles—equality before law, liberty of conscience, speech, press—worked in peace. Bourbons instrument of civilization.

**Revolution of July (1830)**: Hardly produced shock; did not treat vanquished royalty as enemy.

**Louis Philippe (current Spring Year 5)**: Handsome in old age, graceful. Lacked majesty; wore no crown, no white hair. Mixture of noble and bourgeois suited 1830. Incorruptible; went out with umbrella. Policy domestic rather than national; excessive timidity displeasing to people. Deep tenderness toward family. One daughter, Marie d'Orleans. Press free, tribune free, conscience and speech free. **Will remain one of best princes who ever sat on throne.**

**Cloud gathering (Spring Year 5)**: Strange shade drew nearer—shade from wraths and systems. Everything hastily stifled, moving, fermenting. Electric tension such that first comer brought light. Ever since 1830, petty revolts suppressed but ever bursting afresh—sign of vast underlying conflagration.

## English Provincial Towns: Population and Daily Life (Documented)
**Population movements**: Peten Haskick moved to Quenford; Lura Haskick followed. Kadrek moved to Wilholt. Zalis Corrley's daughter settled Wilholt. Kadan Corrley took Yewyn Corrford in marriage at Kelmere. Quiet Jotho married eldest daughter of Fewyn Stenworth at Ostcombe; couple lived there. **That spring, coughing sickness took Nelan; buried at Kelford.** **Taric Corrley quit Kelmere for good (after quarrel), took lodgings in Staveford. Kassa Stenson went along to live in Staveford as well.** Families: Stenworth, Prydenridge, Thornmere, Lindmere, Brackick. **Ulrald Corrford apprenticed anew, became smith.**

**Daily mundane activities (April/ongoing)**: Sorting old letters by candlelight; mending torn sleeves by window, saying little; scrubbing steps while humming. **Yewyn Corrford spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight.** Luena Stenenridge and Rozek Stenenridge talked: "The price of salt is a scandal." Rozek counted coins twice, came up penny short; pressed jade mirror into wife's hands, took nothing; walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Luena laughed at story nobody else found funny. **Elra Corrford laughed at a story nobody else found funny.** Rorald Lindmere mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Weather, harvest, river conditions constant. **Yewyn Corrford and Rorald talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse.** Yewyn bought ribbon at stall, regretted it. Yera read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. **Pelia Lindmere watched clouds, predicted rain, wrongly.** River up in spring; repeated remarks.

## Javert's Outstanding Question
**After M. Leblanc's escape**: Javert did not take prisoner prisoner. **"The assassinated man who flees is more suspicious than the assassin, and it is probable that this personage, who had been so precious a capture for the ruffians, would be no less fine a prize for the authorities."** M. Leblanc's identity and whereabouts remain mystery requiring resolution.
